project.name: Fern rollout
project.brief: Out of Pocket is expanding, fast, and is now running more big projects at once than any newsletter company should. This is one of them. OOP now has about 350 employees across its new divisions, and in 2 weeks every one of them gets Fern, an AI assistant from a company called Fernwood Labs. Fern writes, takes meeting notes, and searches company files. OOP signed a 3-year contract and billing starts Nov 2 whether or not anyone logs in, so the date is not moving. The project tracker says things are mostly on track. Your job is to figure out what's really going on before go-live day

notes.title: Fern go-live readiness
bullets: Harper opened with a 10-minute demo where Fern wrote a haiku about synergy. Applause
Policy, security review, and feature decisions: Gloria is waiting on Leon, Leon is waiting on Harper, Harper is waiting on Gloria. Harper suggested asking Fern to sort it out
Leon stayed for 10 minutes, then left to approve something else. He has 14 connection requests in his queue and a 212-question vendor questionnaire he hasn't read
Logins: 90% done. The last 10% is the 120 people at OOP Revenue, who are on a different login system since the acquisition. That's about a third of the company
Quinn says the shared drive connection is on track. No follow-up questions
Training: Felix says 90% done, the videos just need uploading. They were recorded during the pilot
Two policies are being written, Gloria's and Nadia's. Neither knew about the other until today. Agreed to merge them at some point
ROI: Devi asked how we'll know if this worked. Harper said "vibes, for now." The ticket says TBD until the contract is signed. It was signed 10 weeks ago
Pilot learnings: Felix asked where the write-up is. It's assigned to Bianca, who left in June
Go-live support: nobody owns who answers questions on day one. Theo suggested people ask Fern
Go-live stays Nov 2. Billing starts that day either way
